evidence.positive: Against the running build (ad6fc2319, demo-demo tenant): GET /api/admin/rule/definitions returned 113 registered rules with no id matching /mrsa/ and includes("w-mrsa-infection-status") === false. Staged a demo patient (or2939-fake-54a73ce7..., case 00264) with a p-gastroduodenal case (CEFAZOLIN pathway) and an MRSA_INFECTION observation valued "MRSA POSITIVE" dated 24h earlier via POST /api/admin/observations/patient/{pmrn}/case/{caseId}. POST /api/cds/medication-selection/{pmrn}/{caseId} with medicationIdentifier m-cefazolin returned 200 with results ruleIds ["w-cefazolin-default-dose"] only; GET /api/admin/rule/evaluations/fired?caseId=00264 listed one fired rule (w-cefazolin-default-dose) and the 72 not-fired rows for the case contained no w-mrsa-infection-status entry. The app log held zero lines mentioning w-mrsa-infection-status before the red check.
evidence.negative: The MRSA guidance still reaches the clinician through the OR-2933 replacement, and the citation reassignment in citations.csv holds. On the same MRSA-positive case GET /api/admin/patients/{pmrn}/operations/00264/antibiotic-candidates returned outcome RECOMMENDED with step 1 {mrsaAdjusted: true, medicationCandidates: [CEFAZOLIN, VANCOMYCIN]}. A second patient (or2939neg-fake-2fba55cf..., case 04875) staged with MRSA POSITIVE at -48h followed by "MRSA NOT DETECTED" at -24h got step 1 {mrsaAdjusted: false, [CEFAZOLIN]} and a cefazolin selection again returned only w-cefazolin-default-dose, so the pathway adjustment is driven by live MRSA status, not a leftover of the deleted rule. Selecting m-ertapenem (not on the pathway) on the MRSA-positive case fired a-known-procedure-wrong-antibiotic whose prompt citations were ["r-procedure-wrong-antibiotic","r-mrsa-infection-status"], confirming the r-mrsa-infection-status citation row now serves the surviving rules.
evidence.red_check: Ran the pre-fix code. Took MrsaInfectionStatusWarningRule.java from the parent of 653b7bf61, compiled it inside the app container with javac against /app/classes:/app/libs/* (no lombok needed), copied the .class into /app/classes/com/guided/orci/engine/rule/medication/selection/ (no shipped file existed there to back up: the ticket deletes it), and docker-restarted the container. On boot the log printed "Created feature flag for rule: w-mrsa-infection-status", GET /api/admin/rule/definitions grew to 114 ids including w-mrsa-infection-status, and the identical m-cefazolin selection on case 00264 now returned results ruleIds ["w-cefazolin-default-dose","w-mrsa-infection-status"] with promptText "MRSA positive on 10/26/2026. Consider adding Vancomycin." and citation r-mrsa-infection-status; the log printed "Rule evaluated: w-mrsa-infection-status -> true null". Reverted by deleting the injected .class (ls confirms it is absent), removing the /tmp compile dirs, and docker-restarting again; after the restart the registry is back to 113 without the id, the same selection returns only w-cefazolin-default-dose, and zero log lines after the second "Started OrciApplication" mention w-mrsa-infection-status. The signature string appears exactly once in the whole container log, during the red window.

caveats: Validated through the REST surface the UI renders (medication-selection results and antibiotic-candidates); the banner absence was not viewed in a browser.
Only the demo-demo tenant was exercised; the deleted rule was tenant-agnostic code, so mgb/mayo differ only by their identical citations.csv edit.

The red check left a w-mrsa-infection-status row in demo-demo.rule_definitions and a feature-flag row in this disposable DB (upsert-only sync never prunes); production will likewise keep its historical catalog row, which the spec README retired-rules table already accounts for.

Two backend test files (RuleComplianceServiceGuardTest, MedicationAdministeredComplianceEvaluatorTest) still use the string w-mrsa-infection-status as an arbitrary rule id label; harmless, no runtime reference remains.

automation.assessment: No qa-suite test mentions MRSA. OR-2933 backend tests cover the MRSA-adjusted pathway and the partial citation; nothing locks in the absence of the retired warning on a real selection. Worth one supplemental API-level pair in qa-suite that asserts the warning is gone while the replacement is present, so the absence check cannot pass vacuously.

qa-suite @supplemental: same staging plus a later MRSA NOT DETECTED observation, assert antibiotic-candidates step 1 mrsaAdjusted === false and VANCOMYCIN absent.
qa-suite @supplemental: on the MRSA-positive case select m-ertapenem and assert a-known-procedure-wrong-antibiotic fires with citation r-mrsa-infection-status attached.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: Against the main build, the rule registry no longer lists w-mrsa-infection-status and a cefazolin selection for an MRSA-positive patient on a cefazolin pathway returned only the default-dose warning.
Negative: The same case still gets the MRSA-adjusted first step (cefazolin plus vancomycin) from the OR-2933 pathway, a patient with a later negative result does not, and the wrong-antibiotic alert still carries the MRSA citation.
Red check: Compiling the deleted rule class back into the running container made the same selection fire the retired warning with its MRSA positive on 10/26/2026 text, and removing it restored the absence.

Automation: A supplemental qa-suite API pair is proposed that asserts the warning is absent while the MRSA-adjusted pathway is present.
